scores.evidence: Yjs garbage collection removes deleted content, so the log is the only source for full history.
scores.rationale: Mostly accurate on Yjs/Hocuspocus, awareness, RelativePosition, UndoManager; minor imprecisions (hash compare at same state vector, 'no central sequencer needed', schema-enforced invariants limits) have little design consequence.

scores.evidence: User A opens `/d/<id>` and types "hello". User B, in another browser, sees "hello" in under 500 ms.
scores.rationale: Covers core collaborative editing, persistence, permissions, history, presence with explicit deferrals and triggers; offline limited and some product decisions remain assumed.

scores.evidence: Every client of a given document connects to the same sync node, via consistent-hash routing on the document ID.
scores.rationale: Consistent responsibilities and data ownership; minor loose ends such as 'one node until Phase 3' versus consistent-hash routing and redirects, and the tension between the Phase 0 'hello' slice and Phase 1 schema.

scores.evidence: A seeded property-based fuzz suite runs 10,000 random multi-client edit sequences with dropped, reordered and duplicated messages and server kills mid-commit.
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, including fuzz, divergence detector in prod, restore drill, node-kill chaos, and early end-to-end slice; some thresholds are invented but presented as targets/examples.

scores.evidence: Switch to OT with a server-side sequencer if the product needs server-validated edits that a CRDT can't express
scores.rationale: Decisions have explicit revisit triggers and sensitivity, but scale, team size and budget assumptions are mostly implicit and numbers like 500 editors, 20%, 25% are unsupported.

scores.evidence: Idempotent append. Deduplicate on `(doc_id, client_id, clock)` so retried updates are never applied twice.
scores.rationale: Covers duplicates, divergence, malformed updates, node failure, permission revocation, XSS/upload, slow consumers, with detection and recovery; minor gaps like poisoned CRDT state/undo of malicious large updates.

scores.evidence: Graceful drain on deploy. Stop accepting connections, hand off documents, then close sockets with a reconnect hint.
scores.rationale: Observability, deploy, rollback-of-schema, PITR, alerts are concrete; incident ownership/on-call and rollback of app deploys are thin, and deploy on every merge to prod is aggressive.

scores.evidence: Storage cost passes budget (e.g. more than $X per workspace per month).
scores.rationale: Cost is barely addressed; raw log kept forever is the main growth driver with only a placeholder budget, with no build-cost or run-cost estimates.

scores.evidence: the costliest to reverse, because the stored document format follows it ... Decide before Phase 1 ends.
scores.rationale: Explicitly identifies CRDT choice, schema, E2E, section permissions, subdocuments as one-way, with triggers, isolation and migration paths, and reversible choices decided quickly.

scores.evidence: One codebase, two process roles ... Split further only when one area needs its own scaling or release cadence.
scores.rationale: Adopts libraries and a monolith with deferrals; some ceremony (mTLS, pub/sub circuit breaker, N/A AI sections, row-level tenancy) is slightly speculative.

scores.evidence: Exit check: The "hello" scenario passes in prod, including the server restart.
scores.rationale: Thin vertical slice first, dependency-reasoned phases with exit checks and revisit triggers; a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: CRDT (Yjs). Edits apply locally first, all copies are guaranteed to converge... Switch to OT with a server-side sequencer if the product needs server-validated edits
Define the ProseMirror node and mark set: headings, lists, marks, links. Tables and media come in Phase 6.
A seeded property-based fuzz suite runs 10,000 random multi-client edit sequences with dropped, reordered and duplicated messages
The server confirms an update only after it is durably committed to Postgres... Never delete log rows
Consistent-hash routing of documents to sync nodes... Client reconnects with exponential backoff and jitter... backpressure on slow consumers
The client keeps unconfirmed updates in IndexedDB until they're confirmed, so they survive a tab crash.
Long-lived sockets re-check permission every 5 minutes. Revoking access closes the socket within 60 s.
Per-user undo/redo (Y.UndoManager tracking only local changes).
Presence travels the same path but is never stored.
Phase 2: Convergence and durability hardening ... Phase 6: Rich content and polish (the flashy leaf work)
Histogram of document sizes... Keystroke-to-render p95 stays under 16 ms on a 50-page document.
A protocol version... Servers reject unsupported versions with an "upgrade client" code.

traps.evidence: Adopt: Yjs, y-protocols, ProseMirror/Tiptap, Hocuspocus as the sync-server base.
using the *real* CRDT library rather than a stub.
sends a confirmation only after the commit;
No central sequencer needed for correctness.

note: Strong, risk-driven plan with a thin end-to-end slice on Yjs and durable-before-ack. Weak on cost, with thin coverage of rich-text merge semantics, large-document limits and presence cursor behavior.
